answer: The trail began in karst country, where rain had dissolved the limestone into stone pillars above hidden rivers. We camped beside a stream that ran the colour of copper, stained by old mine workings far upstream. By the third day the forest thinned and the ground hardened into a scrubby tundra plateau, wind-scoured and silent. Nothing dramatic happened the whole week, and that was the point: the landscape simply shifted under our boots, one geology quietly giving way to the next.
